description: Resource-agnostic HTTP core + typed error hierarchy + client config extension. Adds src/errors.ts (base WhatsAppError and subclasses), src/http.ts (HttpClient with timeout/retry/backoff built on global fetch + AbortController), src/types/common.ts (Graph error-envelope type and shared bits), extends WhatsAppClientConfig with optional timeoutMs/maxRetries (backward compatible), and wires an internal HttpClient into WhatsAppClient. This is the foundation FEAT-002 depends on; it knows nothing about messages. Zero runtime deps.
steps: Add src/types/common.ts: a GraphErrorEnvelope type matching { error: { message: string; type?: string; code: number; error_subcode?: number; error_data?: { messaging_product?: string; details?: string }; fbtrace_id?: string } }, plus any shared HTTP types (HttpMethod union, a RequestOptions shape). Use `export interface`/`export type`; respect exactOptionalPropertyTypes (optionals are `?:`, never `| undefined` assigned explicitly).

Add src/errors.ts: base `class WhatsAppError extends Error` setting this.name and supporting an options cause. Subclasses: WhatsAppApiError (fields httpStatus:number, code:number, subcode?:number, type?:string, details?:string, fbtraceId?:string, raw:unknown) for non-2xx with a parseable envelope; WhatsAppAuthenticationError extends WhatsAppApiError for 401/403 or auth codes; WhatsAppRequestError extends WhatsAppError for network/abort/timeout (carries cause, and an isTimeout flag); WhatsAppValidationError extends WhatsAppError for boundary misuse. Export a factory `errorFromResponse(httpStatus, envelope, bodyText?)` that constructs WhatsAppApiError or WhatsAppAuthenticationError (auth when httpStatus is 401/403; key the decision off numeric code/status per Meta guidance). NEVER include the access token in any message. Use `override` where needed; set each name distinctly.

Add src/http.ts: `class HttpClient` constructed with { accessToken, baseUrl (already versioned), timeoutMs, maxRetries }. Method `request<T>({ method, path, body?, signal? }): Promise<T>` that builds the URL as `${baseUrl}/${path}` (strip any leading slash on path), sets Authorization: `Bearer ${accessToken}` and, when a body is present, Content-Type: application/json with JSON.stringify(body); parses the JSON response. Enforce timeout with a fresh AbortController per attempt (combine with any caller signal). On a 2xx parse and return JSON as T. On non-2xx: parse the body, and if it has an `error` object build via errorFromResponse and throw; otherwise throw a generic WhatsAppApiError with the status. Retry policy: retry only on HTTP 429, 5xx, and network/timeout errors, up to maxRetries (default 2 => 3 attempts total); never retry other 4xx and never retry WhatsAppValidationError. Backoff: exponential (base ~300ms, factor 2) with full jitter; when a Retry-After header is present (delta-seconds or HTTP-date) honor it instead. Convert fetch rejections / AbortError into WhatsAppRequestError (isTimeout true for the timeout abort). Make the sleep injectable (e.g. a constructor-overridable or module-level delay function) so tests can use fake timers deterministically. The HTTP layer must NOT reference messages.

Edit src/index.ts: add optional `timeoutMs?: number` and `maxRetries?: number` to WhatsAppClientConfig with JSDoc. In the resolved config apply defaults (timeoutMs 30000, maxRetries 2). Instantiate a private readonly HttpClient from the resolved config (accessToken, getBaseUrl() value, timeoutMs, maxRetries). Expose an internal bound request for resources (e.g. a private method or a readonly bound function) WITHOUT changing any existing public getter or the empty-accessToken guard. Export WhatsAppError and all error subclasses and the common types from the barrel. Preserve exactOptionalPropertyTypes-safe conditional spreads for optional fields.
acceptance_criteria: src/errors.ts, src/http.ts, and src/types/common.ts exist and compile under the strict tsconfig.
WhatsAppClientConfig accepts optional timeoutMs and maxRetries; omitting them keeps prior behavior (defaults 30000/2).
WhatsAppClient instantiates an internal HttpClient and exposes an internal request path for resources, with all existing public getters and the empty-token guard unchanged.
WhatsAppError and all error subclasses plus common types are exported from src/index.ts.
The 6 existing tests in tests/client.test.ts still pass.
No runtime dependency was added (package.json dependencies stays empty).
Running `pnpm run typecheck && pnpm run lint && pnpm run format:check && pnpm run test && pnpm run build` succeeds.
verification: Run `pnpm run typecheck` and confirm no type errors.
Run `pnpm run lint` and confirm no lint errors.
Run `pnpm run format:check` (run `pnpm run format` first if needed) and confirm formatting passes.
Run `pnpm run test` and confirm all tests pass, including the 6 existing client tests.
Run `pnpm run build` and confirm tsup produces dist/index.js, dist/index.cjs and the .d.ts/.d.cts without errors.
findings: Exported from src/index.ts barrel for FEAT-002: error classes WhatsAppError, WhatsAppApiError, WhatsAppAuthenticationError, WhatsAppRequestError, WhatsAppValidationError, and the factory errorFromResponse; type WhatsAppApiErrorFields; common types GraphErrorEnvelope, HttpMethod, RequestOptions; constants DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS (30000) and DEFAULT_MAX_RETRIES (2). HttpClient is defined and exported from src/http.ts (class HttpClient, interface HttpClientConfig) but is NOT re-exported from the barrel (kept internal). Internal request entry point for resources: WhatsAppClient has a public method `request<T>(options: RequestOptions): Promise<T>` (marked @internal) that delegates to the private readonly `http` HttpClient; call it as `client.request<T>({ method, path, body?, signal? })` where path is relative to the versioned base URL (leading slash stripped). Config accessor for phoneNumberId: WhatsAppClient.getPhoneNumberId(): string | undefined (unchanged); getBaseUrl(), getApiVersion(), getBusinessAccountId() also unchanged. HttpClient.request returns parsed JSON as T (or undefined for an empty 2xx body) and throws the typed errors; retries only 429/5xx/network/timeout up to maxRetries, honoring Retry-After. RequestOptions is defined in src/types/common.ts. Note: .agents/tasks/plan.md fails prettier format:check but it is pre-existing untracked workflow metadata, not shipped source; all src/ and tests/ files pass the full gate.
